title: The $500 Millionaire Math

beats.say: Put $500 a month into an index fund at 8% a year, and the math gets wild.
beats.visual: A silhouette of hands sliding a single silver coin across a dark wooden desk, moody side lighting.

beats.say: Most people think it takes a massive salary to build a fortune. But they're missing one hidden rule.
beats.visual: A close up of a brass mechanical gear turning slowly inside an old clock, cinematic macro shot.

beats.say: Let's run the exact numbers for a regular earner starting from scratch.
beats.visual: A vintage metal desk lamp casting a warm glow on a clean stack of blank white paper.

beats.say: After 20 years of investing $500 a month at 8%, you've put in $120,000.
beats.visual: A person's hands wearing a wool sweater counting crisp green bank notes under dim light.

beats.say: That grows into $294,510 through the quiet power of monthly compounding.
beats.visual: A time-lapse shot of shadows moving across a minimalist concrete wall in late afternoon.

beats.say: Wait 10 more years, and it jumps to $745,180 with $180,000 of your own cash.
beats.visual: An overhead shot of a dark coffee cup steaming on a rustic oak table, moody shadows.

beats.say: But here's the part nobody mentions about the final decade.
beats.visual: A close up of a brass pocket watch ticking against a dark textured background.

beats.say: Push that same plan to 40 years, and your total investment hits $240,000.
beats.visual: A silhouette of a person walking away down a long empty industrial hallway.

beats.say: That final sum swells to $1,745,504 without you working a single extra hour.
beats.visual: A macro shot of water droplets falling onto a calm reflective black surface.

beats.say: Time does the heavy lifting while you just stay consistent.
beats.visual: An open window showing a city skyline at dusk with lights flickering on slowly.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you...
beats.visual: A dark minimalist room with a single pencil resting on a blank wooden notebook.

caption:
The math doesn't care about your job title. Time and consistency do the heavy lifting.
